history.request: Build a breakfast shop ordering system with three tabs. Tab 1 "Order": customers pick items (egg crepe $3.50, radish cake $4.00, teppan noodles $5.50, chicken nuggets $4.50, milk tea $3.00, soy milk $2.50), change quantities, enter a table number and send the order. Tab 2 "Kitchen": orders listed by time; each order moves from "To do" to "Cooking" to "Done", each state in its own color. Tab 3 "Sales": today's number of orders and total sales.
history.summary: A breakfast shop ordering system with three tabs. The Order tab lets customers choose menu items, adjust quantities, enter a table number and send the order. The Kitchen tab lists orders by time and lets staff move each one from To do to Cooking to Done, with a distinct color for each state. The Sales tab shows today's order count and total sales. The static web front end talks to a Python standard-library JSON API that keeps all data in memory.

endpoints.purpose: Return the fixed list of menu items with id, name and price.
Create an order from a table number and item quantities; the server computes the total and sets status to todo.
List orders sorted by creation time, optionally filtered by status.
Advance an order from todo to cooking to done.
Return today's number of orders and total sales.

modules.name: server.py
modules.purpose: Single standard-library Python module (http.server) with the menu, in-memory order store, validation, status transitions, sales calculation and JSON routing.

modules.name: index.html
modules.purpose: Page structure with the three tabs (Order, Kitchen, Sales) and their panels.

modules.name: app.js
modules.purpose: Tab switching, API calls, order form logic, kitchen board rendering and sales display.

modules.name: style.css
modules.purpose: Layout, tab styling, menu cards and the distinct colors for To do, Cooking and Done.

plan.notes: Data is kept in memory only, so orders and sales reset when the API restarts. Prices are calculated on the server and stored in cents to avoid rounding errors. 'Today' is based on the API server's local date. Order statuses use the values todo, cooking and done, which the front end displays as To do, Cooking and Done. No authentication is included, so the Kitchen and Sales tabs are visible to everyone who can open the app.
steps: Define the fixed menu in the API: egg crepe $3.50, radish cake $4.00, teppan noodles $5.50, chicken nuggets $4.50, milk tea $3.00, soy milk $2.50.
Implement the in-memory order store in the API module with an incrementing order id, table number, items, quantities, total, status and created time.
Implement GET /menu to return the menu items with id, name and price.

Implement POST /orders with validation: table number is required, at least one item, quantities are positive integers, item ids exist. The server calculates the total from menu prices and sets the status to todo.
Implement GET /orders to return orders sorted by creation time, with an optional status filter.
Implement PATCH /orders/{id}/status to move an order forward only in the sequence todo, then cooking, then done, rejecting invalid transitions.
Implement GET /sales/today to return today's order count and total sales, computed from the orders created today.
Add CORS-free same-origin JSON handling, error responses with clear messages, and a threading lock around the in-memory data.
Build index.html with a header, three tab buttons (Order, Kitchen, Sales) and a content panel for each tab.

Build the Order tab in app.js: load the menu, render items with plus and minus quantity controls, show a running total, take the table number and submit the order, then reset the form and show a confirmation.
Build the Kitchen tab in app.js: fetch orders, list them by time, show table number, items and status, and offer a button to advance each order to the next state. Refresh periodically.
Style the three states in style.css: To do (for example red or orange), Cooking (yellow or amber) and Done (green), applied to badges and card borders.
Build the Sales tab in app.js: fetch /sales/today and show the number of orders and total sales formatted as dollars.
Add tab switching logic that refreshes the data of the selected tab.
Make the layout responsive for phones and tablets used at the counter and in the kitchen.
Test the full flow: place an order, see it in Kitchen as To do, advance it to Cooking and Done, and check that Sales updates.
